newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican labor leader dies aged 97 - reports.
newsitem.headline: Mexican labor leader dies aged 97 - reports.

text.p: Mexican labor leader Fidel Velazquez, who for 60 years headed Mexico's largest labor union and was a pillar of support for the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), died on Saturday at age 97, radio reports said.
Velazquez died in a hospital at 9:20 a.m. (1420 GMT) in Mexico City, Radio Red reported. His death was also reported by main television broadcaster Televisa.
He had been in and out of the hospital several times in recent months and last entered the hospital on June 5 with what his doctor Salomon Jasqui described as a urinary infection.
Velazquez was Mexico's most powerful labor leader and for decades swung workers support behind the ruling PRI, earning him a position as one of the country's most important power brokers.

His death came just as the PRI faces a major test in July 6 mid-term elections and is likely to set off a struggle for his replacement as chief of the 6 million-strong Confederation of Mexican Workers (CTM).
